content.title: Live updates as Portland Fire selects three players in 2026 WNBA Draft
content.text: For the first time since 2002, the Portland Fire are taking part in a WNBA draft. The Fire have the No. 7, 17 and 37 picks in the 2026 draft. The No. 17 pick comes from the Chicago Sky, part of a trade to ensure that Portland didn’t select any Chicago players in the expansion draft. Portland Fire’s selectionsNo. 7: Iyana Martín, Spain No. 17: Frieda Bühner, GermanyNo. 37: Taylor Bigby, TCUTrade: Portland Fire add UConn forward via draft-day trade with Connecticut SunRoster so far Bridget Carleton: A 6-foot-2 forward, Carleton comes to Portland from the Minnesota Lynx. Černivec and coach Alex Sarama both indicated that Carleton has been underutilized in recent years and in Portland she can develop into an All-Star-caliber player. Carla Leite: At just 21 years old, Leite has already proven that she can be an effective point guard in the WNBA. So much so that Černivec has selected her in two straight expansion drafts (going to Golden State last year).Karlie Samuelson: Samuelson was the splashiest signing for the Portland Fire on Saturday, the first day of the WNBA free agency signing period. Samuelson has been in the league since 2017 and will likely be a crucial veteran presence for what is mostly a young roster. Megan Gustafson: Gustafson will likely be a consistent presence in the paint for the Fire in 2026. A 6-foot-4 center, Gustafson was a member of the Las Vegas Aces’ 2025 WNBA Championship roster. She signed with the Fire on Sunday afternoon. Luisa Geiselsöder: A 6-foot-4 center, Geiselsöder was drafted with the Fire’s third pick in the expansion draft and will likely be someone the Fire will lean on in the paint this year. Geiselsöder just won the 2026 EuroCup with ÇBK Mersin. Haley Jones: Jones has jumped from team to team over the past few years, but the Fire signed the former Stanford guard to a one-year contract (as opposed to a training camp contract) which indicates that she may see a bigger role with the team in 2026. Emily Engstler: A 6-foot-1 forward, Engstler was selected fourth in the 2022 WNBA draft by Indiana. She’s never been a consistent starter in the league and was one player Sarama said could develop into a strong contributor. Chloe Bibby: A 6-foot-2 forward, Bibby split time between the Valkyries and the Fever in 2025 (her only season in the WNBA). With Golden State, she averaged 6.4 points per game. Sarah Ashlee Barker: Barker gets the unique distinction of being the first Fire player to touch down in Portland. Selected by the Los Angeles Sparks in 2025, she played in 34 games as a rookie. Maya Caldwell: Caldwell has been in the league for four years and played in a career-high 41 games in 2025 for the Dream. Throughout her career, she’s proven to be a strong rebounder for the guard position. Nyadiew Puoch: Puoch has yet to debut in the WNBA, but she has signed her rookie deal with the Fire and is in town to take part in training camp. The 6-foot-3, 21-year-old forward could be a major boost to the team that is in need of more length. Nika Mühl: Černivec said selecting Mühl in the expansion draft was a personal choice, because the two have known each other for over a decade and crossed paths in European basketball camps. Mühl will be unavailable for the 2026 season due to an ACL injury. Still to be signed Sug Sutton: Sutton remains an unrestricted free agent, but is someone that will likely be a significant rotational player this year (if not the full-time starter at shooting guard). Sutton was a fan-favorite last year with Washington, starting in 43 games and scoring 7.4 points per game. What do the Fire need? After the 2026 expansion draft, Fire general manager Vanja Černivec indicated that finding more post players would be a focal point before the start of the season. So expect Portland to look for a center or a tall forward in the draft. Černivec also indicated that another point guard could be a target. Leite will likely be the starting point guard and the addition of Samuelson will help with depth in the back court. But if the best player available is a guard, don’t be surprised if the Fire decide to bolster that position.
